one_line: Shared parametric hopyard planning with agent-proposed alternatives and human approval.
what_it_does: Calculates hopyard geometry, quantities, costs, preliminary loads, 2D plans, and interactive 3D views while letting an agent read state and create non-destructive alternatives.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared state and non-destructive scenario generation are materially better than asking a general browser agent to operate a complex parametric farm planner.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a live 2D/3D parametric design workspace.
Frame captions describe five structured site tools and creation of Korean L-shaped and North American 18-foot Y alternatives without touching the original.
Agent and farmer are presented as working in the same design space.
execution_rationale: The video evidence shows a coherent workflow from inputs to quantities/costs, 2D plan, 3D inspection, and alternative generation; exact tool payloads are not legible.
execution_evidence: 2D plan visibly contains rows, poles, wires, and anchors.
3D model is shown from multiple angles and zoom levels.
Results panels and captions show cost/material/load calculations and alternatives.
impact_rationale: This addresses a concrete planning problem for hop growers and installers, with useful cost and structural planning outputs and a farmer-controlled decision process.
impact_evidence: Creator packaging identifies hop-farm use and personal farmer motivation.
Visible outputs include construction-oriented layout, material quantities, estimates, and load checks.
creativity_rationale: Human-agent co-design for agricultural structural planning, including inspectable regional alternatives, is a fresh and ambitious application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Non-destructive comparison of distinct training layouts.
Integrated 2D, 3D, engineering, and cost workflow.
usability_note: Clear planner structure and human approval boundary; the dense engineering UI may still require domain familiarity.
red_flags: Exact agent calls and structural correctness are not independently verifiable from the frames.
standouts: Non-destructive alternatives with human decision authority
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with strong end-to-end product-motion evidence.

one_line: Privacy-preserving lost-and-found ownership verification conducted through an agent conversation.
what_it_does: Lets finders record private item details and claimants answer verification questions; the server returns only verified or not verified.
leverage_rationale: Conversation is central to the verification interview, and page-scoped tools let an agent move from search to item-specific verification without receiving the secrets or exposing them to others.
leverage_evidence: About text describes salted hashes/semantic verification and a boolean-only result.
Frames show an agent panel beside the lost-item flow and a transition to Wallet Brown.
Packaging describes changing toolsets as the agent moves between pages.
execution_rationale: The frames show search/item identification and progressive answer selection, but remain at or near the verification form with no unmistakable final success state.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly progress from item search to Wallet Brown and multiple verification controls.
No clearly readable final verified/not-verified result is shown.
Devpost packaging presents the intended flow but is not runtime proof.
impact_rationale: It targets a specific, serious trust problem in lost-and-found communities where public details enable fraudulent claims while private details hinder legitimate recovery.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies lost-item recovery in WhatsApp groups and the proof-versus-secrecy tension.
Visible flow asks ownership questions without displaying the private answer to the platform/agent.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-mediated conversational verification and zero-knowledge-style disclosure minimization is memorable and unusually well matched to the problem.
creativity_evidence: Boolean-only verification rather than revealing which answers matched.
Agent interface is framed as the verification conversation itself.
usability_note: Question flow is approachable, though privacy-sensitive verification needs careful user trust and error handling.
red_flags: Final verification outcome and privacy enforcement are not clearly visible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Agent conversation is not a bolt-on
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and impact; execution evidence is adequate but not fully end-to-end.

one_line: A shared incident console where human and agent investigate production outages on one screen.
what_it_does: Exposes metrics, traces, logs, deploy correlation, pinned findings, rollback proposals, and postmortem drafting through nine page tools, with human approval for rollback.
leverage_rationale: The agent reads and mutates live incident context—time window, trace, filters, findings, and proposed rollback—through structured state rather than trying to infer an observability UI from pixels.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies nine tools and shared screen state.
Claims include get_current_view, metrics/traces/logs, pins, and human-approved rollback.
Frames show a dark structured workflow/trace workspace with status/result blocks.
execution_rationale: The video shows a coherent incident workflow and inspectable tool-oriented interface, though frame text is too small to verify every claimed operation.
execution_evidence: Frames show repeated execution steps, structured outputs, and green/teal result states.
Packaging describes a complete investigation-to-postmortem flow.
Incident console presentation is visually coherent.
impact_rationale: Incident response is a high-value operational use case; shared context and approval boundaries can reduce investigation friction without removing human control.
impact_evidence: Concrete checkout latency incident and production rollback scenario in the description.
Visible incident-console/dashboard workflow and result/status areas.
creativity_rationale: Putting human and agent on the same observability surface, without a chat sidebar, is a strong interaction-model choice for collaborative debugging.
creativity_evidence: One-screen co-debugging premise.
Attribution, exact JSON inspection, and human rollback approval are distinctive details.
usability_note: Shared state and visible ownership should aid handoff; incident tooling remains inherently dense.
red_flags: No public repository and exact tool names/results are not legible in the contact sheets.
standouts: Explicit safety boundary for production rollback
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and credible operational impact with strong product-motion evidence.

one_line: A safety-bounded agent hunt for unowned abnormal labs in OpenMRS.
what_it_does: Finds unowned abnormal results, stages follow-up drafts, and leaves the only chart write to human confirmation through an OpenMRS adapter.
leverage_rationale: Structured read/search and staged-write tools make repetitive multi-chart lab follow-up more reliable while preserving a human confirmation boundary.
leverage_evidence: Frames/package show agent activity, hunt unlabeled abnormal labs, and a review queue.
Visible packaging states the agent hunts while the human confirms the only chart write.
OpenMRS adapter and browser-registered tools are identified.
execution_rationale: The evidence shows a coherent hunt-to-review-queue workflow and a DONE state, but does not show a confirmed chart write end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Packaging thumbnail visibly shows 12 unlabeled abnormal labs and review queue.
Frames show structured multi-step workflow and populated output/status areas.
No final human-confirmed write is visible.
impact_rationale: Reducing missed abnormal-lab follow-up in resource-constrained clinics is a concrete, high-stakes operational benefit, and the safety boundary is appropriate.
impact_evidence: Description grounds the problem in existing OpenMRS workflows and clinician administrative burden.
Visible workflow focuses on unowned abnormal labs and human-confirmed follow-up.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP as a safe operational layer over an existing EMR, rather than attempting diagnosis, is thoughtful and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Agent hunt plus draft queue rather than autonomous chart mutation.
Works with legacy/open-source EMR constraints.
usability_note: Queue-and-confirm pattern is understandable; clinical deployment would require strong permissions and validation.
red_flags: Clinical safety and actual write enforcement require deeper runtime verification.
advance_reason: High impact and strong safety-aware leverage, with credible demonstrated workflow.

one_line: An agent builds, queries, navigates, and exports a live data-grounded map on the visible canvas.
what_it_does: Turns natural-language geographic questions into fetched-data maps, supports layer queries/mutations, zoom, undo, and image export.
leverage_rationale: WebGL canvas state is largely inaccessible to generic agents; structured tools expose rendered layers, counts, camera, filters, queries, and mutations directly.
leverage_evidence: Frames show map viewport changes, query/filter panels, markers, and selected-location popup.
Description names build_map, query_features, zoom_to_layer, export_image, mutate_map, and undo.
Agent actions visibly change the live map and result layer.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence visibly progresses from map interaction to a populated result layer and selected marker; export is claimed but not clearly shown.
execution_evidence: Map moves across regions through successive states.
Final state contains many colored markers and an open result/filter panel.
Tool/action logs are visible alongside the canvas.
impact_rationale: It serves analysts, planners, educators, and ordinary users who need grounded geographic answers without manually assembling map layers.
impact_evidence: Description gives a concrete school/catchment example.
Frames show real-looking geographic visualization with returned point data.
creativity_rationale: Treating the map canvas as a shared agent-readable state and exposing reversible map edits is a strong, memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Canvas-legibility problem is directly addressed.
Build/query/mutate/undo/export workflow is integrated.
usability_note: Natural-language map building lowers GIS friction; credit limits and complex results may still need explanation.
red_flags: Exact fetched sources and export completion are not visible in the sheets.
standouts: Excellent fit between WebMCP and an opaque WebGL canvas
advance_reason: Strongest WebMCP delta among map products and clear visible result state.

one_line: A privacy-scoped browser extension gives agents structured read access to legacy Austrian insurance claims.
what_it_does: Adds page-local claim listing, lookup, search, and year/status tools to existing OEGK pages without changing the government application.
leverage_rationale: It converts a multi-portal, spreadsheet-like claims tracking task into bounded structured reads while keeping the legacy UI and user account in place.
leverage_evidence: Frames show WebMCP claim-status and single-year search actions with populated open-claims lists.
Description identifies read-only query tools and privacy-scoped extension behavior.
Developer/agent console visibly accompanies returned claim data.
execution_rationale: The video shows the claims form, WebMCP actions, console activity, open/reimbursed claims, and a read-only final state.
execution_evidence: Visible action banners include checking claim status and searching a year with one WebMCP call.
Open claims and reimbursed claims are populated in later states.
Console trace is present throughout.
impact_rationale: Managing reimbursement status across government and private insurance workflows addresses a common administrative burden, especially without requiring institutional replacement.
impact_evidence: Description describes manual cross-portal tracking and spreadsheet work.
Frames show claims results returned from a legacy-style interface.
creativity_rationale: The extension-as-agent-bridge approach is practical and socially useful, with privacy scope treated as a core design constraint.
creativity_evidence: Leaves government app unchanged.
Local, bounded, read-only bridge and consolidated year search.
usability_note: Structured retrieval simplifies a fragmented workflow, but account/login and insurance terminology remain burdens.
red_flags: Frames depict a fictional/demo claims environment; real OEGK integration and privacy properties are not independently verified.
advance_reason: Demonstrates a credible, end-to-end bridge with meaningful real-world utility.

one_line: Community accessibility observations become searchable and comparable by agents before a trip.
what_it_does: Stores structured access details and photos for places, lets agents search/compare evidence, and supports updates while preserving uncertainty.
leverage_rationale: Structured accessibility attributes and explicit unknowns make agent answers more reliable than scraping prose reviews, though general agents could still access much of the site with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description lists ten structured accessibility categories and an explicit do-not-guess principle.
Packaging claims agent search, comparison, and keeping data current.
Frames show a travel/accessibility-oriented workflow, but exact tool calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The packet supports the product concept and agent-oriented interface, but the frames do not clearly show a completed venue search or update result.
execution_evidence: Contact sheets show repeated agent/workflow states and structured outputs.
Devpost packaging identifies accessibility data and the intended agent functions.
Specific returned venue evidence is not legible.
impact_rationale: Knowing whether a venue is actually usable before traveling is a specific, high-value need for people with mobility and other access requirements.
impact_evidence: Description details step-free entry, doors, parking, routes, restrooms, seating, and other practical attributes.
Project tagline directly frames pre-visit decision support.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong synthesis of community mapping, structured uncertainty, and agent search, though the category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Ten-category observations and first-class unknown state.
Agent comparison of real-world accessibility evidence.
usability_note: Structured filters can reduce uncertainty; data freshness and inconsistent community coverage are ongoing usability concerns.
red_flags: Low-resolution frames do not establish an end-to-end search/update outcome.
standouts: Honest handling of unknown accessibility facts
advance_reason: Very strong impact and thoughtful data model, despite moderate execution evidence.

one_line: An evidence-first workspace lets humans and agents research, challenge, and decide against shared provenance-rich state.
what_it_does: Organizes questions, sources, claims, evidence links, counterarguments, confidence, gaps, comparisons, and decisions in an inspectable workspace.
leverage_rationale: Stable IDs, provenance relationships, attribution, and explicit evidence semantics are difficult to preserve through generic UI automation; WebMCP is the collaboration layer.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly contrasts WebMCP with copy/paste and DOM automation.
Frames show claims, sources, evidence links, open questions, commentary, and decision cards.
Workflow includes research, challenge, revise, compare, decide.
execution_rationale: The evidence shows a broad but coherent research workflow with source gathering, linking, unresolved gaps, commentary, and decision framing; final decision selection is not always visible.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show populated claims/sources/evidence workspace.
Netlify documentation is gathered as research evidence for a hosting decision.
Controls support refresh, prompt copying, and inspection.
impact_rationale: Inspectable research and decision provenance addresses a real weakness of chat-based research for teams, analysts, and consequential choices.
impact_evidence: Visible question asks a concrete deployment-risk decision.
Product description names durable evidence, confidence changes, counterarguments, and decisions.
creativity_rationale: The product turns agent research from a transient answer into a shared, adversarially inspectable decision process, pursued deeply across the workflow.
creativity_evidence: Attack/challenge-conclusion workflow.
Claims-to-source evidence graph with confidence and research gaps.
usability_note: Inspectable structure supports trust, but the many entities and research controls create a learning curve.
red_flags: The final hosting recommendation is not clearly visible; some tool names are unreadable.
standouts: Research challenge loop rather than answer generation
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity with substantial visible workflow evidence.

one_line: A WebMCP audit scores whether a human-oriented site can be found, understood, and used by agents.
what_it_does: Audits a public URL, reports discovery/structure/renderability/forms/actionability/WebMCP checks, suggests fixes, and generates a tool from the target page’s first form.
leverage_rationale: The audit itself uses a declared page tool to evaluate agent readiness and produces concrete WebMCP remediation, making the agent the target user rather than a UI bolt-on.
leverage_evidence: Description names audit_site and generated WebMCP tool code/schema.
Frames show an audit request progressing to a scored results dashboard.
Visible score gauge and categorized findings support structured output.
execution_rationale: The video visibly progresses from audit setup to a completed dashboard with score, findings, and recommendations, though exact target interactions are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show prompt/setup, agent progress, and final report dashboard.
Packaging preview shows 75/100 grade B with find/understand/act dimensions.
Result includes categorized findings and remediation-style sections.
impact_rationale: It gives developers a fast, actionable way to find why their public sites fail agent tasks and how a WebMCP tool could improve them.
impact_evidence: Clear developer audience and agent-readiness problem.
Output includes a score, top findings, fixes, and computed WebMCP uplift.
creativity_rationale: Auditing agent usability while generating the next site’s WebMCP surface creates a self-reinforcing adoption loop and is ambitious for a hackathon.
creativity_evidence: AgentReady is itself a WebMCP app.
Generates declarative tool attributes, registration code, and JSON schema from audited forms.
usability_note: A single score plus prioritized fixes is approachable; audit methodology and false positives need explanation.
red_flags: Exact checks and target-site completion are not readable in every frame.
advance_reason: Clear developer value, visible end-to-end audit result, and strong WebMCP-specific ambition.

one_line: Families co-create editable pixel-art storybooks with an AI agent through inspectable canvas operations.
what_it_does: Creates stories, reusable sprites, layered scenes, presentation views, sharing/gallery outputs, and page exports while the family directs the narrative.
leverage_rationale: Structured canvas state, reusable assets, and deliberate painting passes let an agent perform precise repeatable artwork while humans retain narrative and art direction; generic UI driving would be much less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Frames show editor, asset/layer panels, preview/present mode, and share/finalization states.
Description says the agent reads storybook state, creates sprites, paints passes, stamps layered scenes, and inspects PNG feedback.
Visible result is a rendered editable story page, not just a prompt response.
execution_rationale: The sequence shows a coherent artifact moving through editing, presentation, sharing/loading, and final preview, though only one clearly legible story page is shown.
execution_evidence: Milo’s Camping Night is consistently rendered with title, tent, fire, characters, and stars.
Editor controls and reusable asset/page-layer setup are visible.
Presentation mode and a final modal/save-share style state are shown.
impact_rationale: It serves families seeking collaborative creative screen time and lowers the barrier to making, revising, and sharing a personal storybook.
impact_evidence: Description identifies children/families and shared creative control.
Frames show an editable/shareable artifact and presentation flow.
creativity_rationale: The concept goes beyond image generation into family-directed, agent-assisted pixel craft with reusable assets and inspectable layered composition.
creativity_evidence: Collaborative storymaking rather than opaque prompt-to-image handoff.
Pixel-art sprites, layered scenes, and iterative PNG feedback.
usability_note: Presentation/share affordances are clear and family-friendly; editor complexity may need age-appropriate guidance.
red_flags: The frame sheets do not clearly show multiple completed pages or exact agent tool calls.
advance_reason: Memorable concept with a visible editable artifact and a meaningful agent role.
